meta.title: SIGIL · Gesture and voice control for your phone, on device
meta.description: Sigil pilots your phone with signs drawn in the air and with your voice. Hand tracking, speech and the language model run on the phone, and nothing leaves it.
og.title: SIGIL · Draw a sign. The phone obeys.
og.description: A companion for Android and iOS that turns hand gestures and voice into actions, fully on device, and asks before it sends anything.
og.imageAlt: A hand draws the SIGIL sign in light above a phone whose front camera tracks it.

hero.title: Draw a sign. The phone obeys.
hero.lead: Sigil pilots your phone with signs drawn in the air and with your voice. Everything it sees and hears stays on the phone.
hero.apkNote: Preview APK. Live hand tracking is on its way.
hero.art.alt: A hand, rim lit in aqua, draws the SIGIL sign in light. Its fingertip is the point of light. Below, the front camera of a phone tracks it.
sign.title: Four ways to read the mark
sign.s1.p: Two strokes around a point of light. The spine is never drawn: the light is the spine.
sign.s2.p: A fingertip closing on a point, the way a thumb and an index finger meet in a pinch.
sign.s3.p: The point follows your index finger across the screen, and it is the core of the Control Sphere.
sign.s4.h: Turn it. It stays the same.
sign.s4.p: Half a turn leaves the sign unchanged, as a seal should. Its Latin root, sigillum, means a small seal.
how.title: From a sign in the air to a tap on the screen.
how.lead: Three stages, and every one of them runs on the phone.
how.fig.alt: A music app on a phone. The holographic cursor sweeps in as a trail of light and snaps onto the Play button, which lights up as a glass lens.
how.s1.title: The camera sees your hand.
how.s1.text: The front camera finds 21 points on your hand, 30 to 60 times a second. Frames are read in memory and dropped.
how.s2.title: Gestures become intents.
how.s2.text: A small classifier reads poses and motion: a pinch, a flick, a circle in the air. The app in front decides what each sign means.
how.s3.title: Actions run.
how.s3.text: The cursor snaps onto targets, so a pinch lands where you aimed. Anything that sends, posts or pays waits for your yes.
how.pipe.label: From camera to action
gestures.title: 14 signs, one hand.
gestures.lead: Every sign is drawn palm toward the camera, the way it sees you. Each one also has a touch path and a voice path.
gestures.note: No sign fires while your hand reaches for the screen, while two hands overlap or within 300 ms of the last one. Losing your hand never commits an action.
g.openPalm.name: Open palm
g.openPalm.when: Five fingers out, palm to the camera, held still for 400 ms. A faint ring grows where the sphere will open.
g.openPalm.does: Opens the Control Sphere over the app you are using.
g.point.name: Point
g.point.when: Index finger out and the other fingers curled, for 200 ms.
g.point.does: Shows the cursor, which follows your fingertip across the screen.
g.pinch.name: Pinch
g.pinch.when: Thumb and index tips meet, then open again within 300 ms.
g.pinch.does: Taps where the cursor is. The press lands where you aimed 90 ms earlier, before your fingers began to close.
g.doublePinch.name: Double pinch
g.doublePinch.when: Two pinches within 350 ms, close together.
g.doublePinch.does: Double tap: opens, zooms or likes, depending on the app.
g.pinchHold.name: Pinch and hold
g.pinchHold.when: The pinch stays closed for 500 ms.
g.pinchHold.does: Long press. Move while you hold to drag. In YouTube, play or pause.
g.fist.name: Fist
g.fist.when: All fingers curl, like holding a microphone.
g.fist.does: Starts listening for a request. With the sphere open, it closes the sphere.
g.swipeUp.name: Two finger swipe up
g.swipeUp.when: Index and middle finger together, a quick move up.
g.swipeUp.does: Scrolls down to what is below.
g.swipeDown.name: Two finger swipe down
g.swipeDown.when: The same two fingers, a quick move down.
g.swipeLeft.name: Two finger swipe left
g.swipeLeft.when: The same two fingers, a quick move to the left.
g.swipeLeft.does: Scrolls sideways. In YouTube, the next video.
g.swipeRight.name: Two finger swipe right
g.swipeRight.when: The same two fingers, a quick move to the right.
g.swipeRight.does: Scrolls sideways. In YouTube, the previous video.
g.threeFingers.name: Three finger swipe
g.threeFingers.when: Index, middle and ring finger together, then a swipe.
g.threeFingers.does: Left goes back, up goes home, right shows recent apps and down opens notifications.
g.circleCw.name: Circle clockwise
g.circleCw.when: The fingertip draws most of a circle in the air, like turning a dial.
g.circleCcw.name: Circle counterclockwise
g.circleCcw.when: The same dial, turned the other way.
g.flick.name: Flick
g.flick.when: A short, fast move of the fingertip that stops.
g.flick.does: Swipes in that direction: the next Reel, the next Short, a notification out of the way.
sphere.title: Open your palm. The sphere answers.
sphere.lead: A glass orb opens where your hand is, over the app you are using, with the actions that make sense right now.
sphere.fig.alt: The Control Sphere: a glass orb with the point of light at its core, a status ring and six quick actions on an orbit. Done is lit under the cursor, the app sits above and recent people below.
sphere.s1.p: After 400 ms of stillness the orb blooms where your hand is. Saying “Sigil” works too.
sphere.s2.h: Six actions, picked by the app.
sphere.s2.p: In Messages: Reply, Read aloud and Done. Recent people sit below the orbit, initials only.
sphere.s3.p: The cursor snaps onto the action. Experts flick toward it without looking.
sphere.summon.title: Summon
sphere.summon.text: Hold an open palm still for 400 ms, say “Sigil”, or long press the edge of the screen.
sphere.choose.title: Choose
sphere.choose.text: Point and pinch, or pinch the core and flick toward an action without looking. You can also say its name or touch it.
sphere.dismiss.title: Dismiss
sphere.dismiss.text: Close your fist, swipe down with two fingers or say “Sigil, close”. With no hand and no voice for 8 seconds, it closes on its own.
sphere.states.title: The mark in motion
sphere.states.label: Sphere state
sphere.state.idle.text: Breathing: one slow breath every 5.2 seconds.
sphere.state.listening.text: The arcs open by 8 degrees and pulse with your voice. Follow ups need no wake word for 8 seconds.
sphere.state.thinking.text: The arcs orbit the point, one turn every 1.6 seconds. After 1.2 seconds the caption reads “Working on it.”
sphere.state.done.text: The point brightens once and settles in 320 ms.
sphere.states.reduced: With reduced motion the mark holds still, and the label carries the state.
profiles.title: Each app speaks its own language.
profiles.lead: Sigil knows which app is in front and loads its profile. A flick moves to the next Reel in Instagram, and a two finger swipe skips to the next video in YouTube. Apps without a profile use the general one.
profiles.fig.alt: Three glass cards for Reader, Music and Camera, each mapping gestures to actions for that app. The Music profile is active and lit in front.
profiles.fig.caption: The profile switches with the app in front.
profiles.inherit: Every app profile starts from these bindings
profiles.row.swipeUpDown: Two finger swipe up or down
profiles.row.swipeLeftRight: Two finger swipe left or right
profiles.wa.r1: Swipe right from the cursor, to reply to that message
profiles.wa.note: Everything else comes from the general profile. Voice plans use the search field, the message box and the send button of WhatsApp, and still stop before sending.
profiles.ig.note: Everything else comes from the general profile.
profiles.yt.note: Everything else comes from the general profile.
profiles.gen.note: Apps without their own profile use these bindings.
profiles.code.caption: One JSON file per app, checked against a schema at startup. No gesture can send, post or pay on its own.
voice.title: Say it once. Watch every step.
voice.lead: Make a fist or say “Sigil”, then ask. The request becomes a short plan of visible steps, and the plan stops before anything leaves your phone.
voice.fig.alt: The Control Sphere listens on the left. The voice leaves it as a wave that settles into a line of light through four glass nodes: open Messages, find Ana, write the note, send.
voice.stage.ask: Send to Ana? Pinch to confirm.
voice.s1.p: “Tell Ana I am running ten minutes late.” Speech becomes text on the phone.
voice.s2.p: The request becomes a chain of steps. Each node lights only when its step really completes.
voice.s3.p: Before Send, the chain stops and asks. A pinch, a touch or “yes” continue, and 8 seconds of silence cancel.
voice.demo.title: Try the chain
voice.demo.request: “Sigil, send Ana on WhatsApp that I am on my way.”
voice.demo.s4: Send to Ana? Pinch to confirm.
voice.demo.note: A simulation in your browser. On the phone, the same plan runs inside WhatsApp, one visible step at a time.
voice.rule.title: The confirmation rule
voice.rule.lead: Never sends or posts without your confirm.
voice.rule.1: Sending, posting, calling, paying, deleting and changing settings always stop for an explicit yes.
voice.rule.2: 8 seconds without an answer cancel. Nothing is ever confirmed by timeout.
voice.rule.3: One message to one person per request. No loops, no schedules, no bulk.
voice.rule.4: Say “Sigil, stop” at any step and the rest is canceled.
privacy.title: Seen by your phone. Kept by your phone.
privacy.lead: Hand tracking, speech recognition and the language model run on the phone. No account, no server, no recording.
privacy.fig.alt: A phone holds a glowing neural sphere. Camera frames from the left and a voice wave from the right flow in and stay inside. The cloud sits outside, marked not needed.
privacy.fig.caption: Camera frames and voice flow in and stay in. The cloud is not needed.
privacy.f1.title: Frames stay in memory
privacy.f1.text: Camera frames are processed and dropped. Only 42 numbers per frame, the points of your hand, reach the interface.
privacy.f2.title: The wake word stays local
privacy.f2.text: The keyword spotter runs on the phone and keeps discarding the audio that comes before the word.
privacy.f3.title: No account, no analytics
privacy.f3.text: Nothing on your screen is uploaded, logged or counted. Tuning data stays on the phone.
privacy.f4.title: The camera never hides
privacy.f4.text: A tracking chip stays on screen while the camera runs. One tap or the words “camera off” stop it.
privacy.tiers.title: A model sized to your phone.
privacy.tiers.text: Sigil picks the largest tier that fits in 35 percent of the phone’s memory. Models download only with your consent, on Wi-Fi by default, and are verified before use.
privacy.tiers.caption: Model tiers by phone memory
privacy.tiers.rules.models: Hand tracking, the system speech recognizer and a rule parser for English and Portuguese
privacy.tiers.lite.models: Hand tracking, Whisper base and Qwen2.5 1.5B
privacy.tiers.full.models: Hand tracking, Whisper small and Qwen2.5 3B
platforms.title: Honest about the platform.
platforms.lead: Controlling other apps is possible only on Android. On iPhone, Sigil works inside its own screens and through Shortcuts, and says so.
platforms.android.title: Full control.
platforms.android.text: Through an Accessibility service you turn on yourself, Sigil taps, swipes, scrolls, types and goes back, home or to recent apps in any app. The cursor is drawn over every app, and the camera keeps running with a visible notification you can stop.
platforms.android.b1: Declared as an accessibility tool for hands free control
platforms.android.b2: Turned on by you, in Settings, Accessibility
platforms.android.b3: Acts only where you point and only when you ask
platforms.ios.title: Inside Sigil, and through Shortcuts.
platforms.ios.text: iOS does not let an app read, tap or draw over other apps, or use the camera in the background. On iPhone, Sigil tracks your hand inside its own screens, opens apps and searches through links, runs your Shortcuts and offers its actions as App Intents to the Shortcuts app and the Action button.
platforms.ios.b1: Gestures, cursor and sphere inside Sigil
platforms.ios.b2: Voice plans through links and Shortcuts
platforms.ios.b3: Steps iOS cannot run are reported as failed, never faked

follow.title: Built in the open.
follow.lead: Sigil is in development. The gesture engine, app profiles, planner and confirmation policy are written and tested. Live hand tracking is next.
follow.hint: Preview builds for Android are on GitHub Releases. If Android asks, allow restricted settings for Sigil in its app info before turning on the accessibility service.

follow.m1.text: Gesture engine with tests, app profiles, planner, confirmation policy, plan executor and the Android control module.
follow.m2.title: Live hands
follow.m2.text: MediaPipe hand tracking on the camera, calibrated for each person.
follow.m3.title: Android end to end
follow.m3.text: Gestures and plans acting in WhatsApp, YouTube, TikTok and Chrome on real phones.
